pr.body:
Refs STREAM-266

Compression helped a lot bring the time on the main thread down. We now think we can scale down the consumers. However, we also need to ensure the flusher can keep up. So let's make the flusher spawn a process per redis shard. 

We think this is easier to do than making the process_spans/insert_spans multiprocessed. Over time we can offload mroe things like statistics/metrics to the flusher, and keep the main thread minimal.
pr.title: ref(span-buffer): Introduce multiprocessed flusher

raw_findings.body: isinstance(spawn_process, multiprocessing.Process) evaluates to False because SpawnProcess is not a subclass of the default-context Process class, so process.kill() is skipped; the old hung process keeps running while _create_process_for_shards spawns a new one for the same shards, leaking processes and potentially producing duplicate segments for those shards.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dead/hung flusher processes are never terminated before restart, causing process leaks and duplicate shard flushing.
raw_findings.impact: isinstance(spawn_process, multiprocessing.Process) evaluates to False because SpawnProcess is not a subclass of the default-context Process class, so process.kill() is skipped; the old hung process keeps running while _create_process_for_shards spawns a new one for the same shards, leaking processes and potentially producing duplicate segments for those shards.
raw_findings.root_cause: The restart path was rewritten to add an isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard that does not match SpawnProcess instances produced by the spawn context.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the kill on the actual base process type (e.g. isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)) or on `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`, so spawn processes are still killed while threads are skipped.
raw_findings.title: Newly added isinstance guard prevents killing hung spawn flusher processes
raw_findings.trigger: A flusher child process created via mp_context (multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, i.e. a SpawnProcess) hangs or dies and _ensure_processes_alive tries to restart it.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use an unpatched delay (e.g. a real sleep helper saved before monkeypatching, or poll for the expected message) instead of the patched time.sleep, or remove the ineffective sleep and rely on join semantics.

finding.verifier_reason: The claim that SpawnProcess is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process is incorrect. In Python's multiprocessing module, multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess IS a subclass of multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess, and isinstance(spawn_process, multiprocessing.Process) returns True because multiprocessing.Process is an alias that resolves correctly. The patch context at line 105 shows make_process = self.mp_context.Process, and the isinstance check at line 254 will work correctly for spawn context processes.

finding.trigger: test_basic runs with monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None) applied, then calls time.sleep(0.1) to 'give flusher threads time to process'.
finding.verifier_reason: The monkeypatch at line 15 patches 'time.sleep' as a string path, which patches the time module's sleep function globally. However, line 62 calls time.sleep(0.1) using the imported time module reference from line 1. The monkeypatch.setattr('time.sleep', ...) patches the module attribute, so time.sleep calls will use the patched version. However, the test still works because step.join() provides synchronization. The sleep is indeed a no-op but the test relies on join() for correctness, making this a minor style issue not a test gap.
